question.text: The value of a for which sum of the squares of the roots of the equation $x^2-(a-2) x-a-1=0$ assumes the least value is

solution.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots, then
$\begin{aligned}
&\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2 \alpha \beta \\
&=(a-2)^2+2(a+1) \\
&=a^2-2 a+6 \\
&=(a-1)^2+5 \geq 5 \\
&\therefore \alpha^2+\beta^2 \text { is minimum if } a=1 .
\end{aligned}$
